summary:
Role C2 (JIT and fuzz tests) is complete. I wrote 9 new repo files, all LF with no CR bytes, and touched no other file. Nothing was committed and nothing was written under build/ or serializer/.

On the B reference (r3/b/bB, md5 702b747a17d5), measured:
- run-bitjit.sh at default size passes in 40 s. Generator: 4 seeds x 2000 loops, 5 JIT option sets x 2 closure modes against -joff, plus the PUC twin: 0 differences. Floor: t_rec, 4 seeds x 3 option sets, 0; t_jit2, 6 option sets, 0, and PUC with X equals -joff in 26/26 loops. fix1: 8/8 loops compile.
- run-bitfuzz.sh passes on seeds 1-4 and in strict mode. The three controls behave: sim-raw and sim-round each fail in exactly the INEXACT tuples (seed 1: 5159).

Fail-firsts, measured:
- Today's b0 fails the generator, t_rec, t_jit2 and the fuzzer (12198 mismatches).
- A's b1, which lacks fix1, fails fix1 with 7 of 8 loops blacklisted, and its PUC twin differs in 1179-1223 cases per seed.
- The generator at default size catches all three B sabotage builds and WBAND, WADD0, WSHL0 in every seed. Minimum differing cases per seed: selfguard 634, w55 199, shr 89, wband 13, wadd0 14, wshl0 30.
- WSHL0 needed no new template: the reviewer's gen.lua already has the boundary template (`((a >> 42) << 32)`, ORed with low bits).

Design changes I made:
- t_jit2 had lost its teeth under B. Seven loops raise early, raises printed no iteration, and guard-exit never compiled. I rebuilt it. It now has 27 loops, reports the iteration of each raise, keeps one X-wrapped text from which both dialects are derived mechanically (with a self-check), hoists guard-exit's closure, adds -b variants of the loops that raise early, and adds narrow-entry to catch NARROW.
- The fuzzer's coverage gate drops from 0.5 to 0.25 and now also covers the U loops. Under B, bB compiles 40-44% of the H loops; the A prototype compiled 61%.

test/native/run-bitfuzz.sh (NEW, 196 lines, md5 e382524c3cdf): written in run-packfuzz.sh's form. A '#cov' line on stderr gives cases, starts, errors, errors past iteration 60, traced cases, traces and aborts (via jit.attach).

test/native/bitop/t_rec.lua (NEW, 95 lines, md5 a8509153d54b): the code is identical to r3/synth/probes/t_rec.lua (diff: comment lines only). The header is rewritten for B and records the re-check counts.

test/native/bitop/t_jit2.lua (NEW, 352 lines, md5 dd47c1675fd5): rebuilt for B, 27 loops (26 run on PUC; sar is LuaJIT-only). Each chunk is f(400, out) with one result per iteration and ERR@<iteration>:<kind>. One X-wrapped text: ours drops the X's; PUC's becomes X(e, '<op>'). A mechanical check (each X wraps exactly one operator at its top level, and the operator count equals the X count) gives INSTRUMENT and exit 2 on failure.

test/native/bitop/p4v.lua (NEW, 95 lines, md5 282f263b5eb2): the reviewer's 8 p4 loops, each run 3 x 100000 iterations. Checks: stop events in the loop's function (at least 1), TYPEINS aborts (via the 'persistent type instability' text in vmdef.traceerr; must be 0), and the loop's opcode via jit.util.funcbc (must be JFORL, not IFORL). No timing. Exit 0/1/2.

test/native/bitop/bitfuzz.lua (NEW, 414 lines, md5 4f13cd884dd5): synth fuzzer with the same PRNG and cases. REF is per-operator X(r, op). Sides: puc, ours, sim-wrap, sim-raw, sim-round (sim-rta/sim-rtz removed). Error kind E:INEXACT:<op>; F13 pattern kept. Startup asserts check X's boundaries and errkind.

test/native/bitop/bitfuzz-cmp.lua (NEW, 166 lines, md5 11c41ed097dd): classes EXACT/INEXACT (was ROUNDED); TIES removed. New self-check: REF ~= RAW exactly where REF is E:INEXACT, else exit 2. hotmin defaults to 0.25 and applies to both H and U loops.

deviations: t_jit2.lua was rebuilt, not just re-checked. Under B, 7 of the 20 A-era loops raise at or before iteration 71. The old format printed a raise without its iteration, and as a result missed NARROW (measured). guard-exit never compiled: -jv shows 'NYI: bytecode FNEW', so design-B's 'NOINT-JIT [t_jit2 guard-exit]' was not true of the old file. Changes: one result per iteration plus ERR@<iteration>:<kind>; the closure hoisted out of the loop; -b variants of count-range, near-2p63, kfold, rotate-round, rec-m53 and rec-grow, with every result exact; rec-m54's mask changed from 0x3fffffffffffff (54 bits, a LEX deviation) to 0x3ffffffffffffe with a body that raises at 208; narrow-entry added. Its PUC comparison uses an X-wrapped single text with a mechanical consistency check, so no second copy is written by hand.

The fuzzer's coverage gate default is 0.25 (was 0.5) and also gates the U loops (hotU). Reason: under B, bB compiles 40-44% of the H loops [M], because the recorder aborts any trace whose recording iteration meets a raising result. 0.25 separates bB from nyi (5-7%).

drv.lua prints ERR@<it>:<kind> instead of ERR@<it>. gen.lua's PUC twin passes the operator to X, so the PUC comparison also checks the error kind and the operator named. gen.lua's chunks return an iteration converter so the 'raised after iteration 60' count uses real iteration counts. The loop variable is not the iteration count for 4 of the 6 loop headers, so counting from the printed value would have been wrong.

Added to the generator part: a trace-coverage gate (a trace in at least 25% of loops, else PROVED NOTHING). The design asked only for a coverage line. Without the gate, a JIT that records no bit operator passes the generator vacuously (nyi: 0 differences).

Fuzzer controls are now sim-wrap, sim-raw and sim-round; sim-rta, sim-rtz and the TIES count are removed. The ROUNDED class is renamed INEXACT. The comparator self-check REF ~= RAW exactly where REF is E:INEXACT is new.

run-bitfuzz.sh keeps every seed's files by default; OCLJ_BITFUZZ_PRUNE=1 opts in to deleting them. run-packfuzz.sh prunes passing seeds automatically. I followed design.md §9: delete only if the user agrees.
run-bitjit.sh adds OCLJ_BITJIT_PARTS (so negctl can run one part) and OCLJ_BITJIT_GENMODE=phi (the reviewer's PHI-heavy mix). Defaults: 4 seeds x 2000 loops, plain mode.
No WSHL0 boundary template was added: the reviewer's gen.lua already has one, and WSHL0 is caught in 30-33 cases per seed.
open_questions: For C3 (negctl-bitop.sh), catchers I measured. NARROW: t_rec (29-55 per seed, every option set) and the generator (11-24 per seed) are robust. t_jit2's narrow-entry caught it in jon and ms0 in 2 of 2 runs and in hl1 in 1 of 2, so gate t_jit2 on 'nonzero in some option set', never on a count. NOINT-JIT: t_jit2 guard-exit and guard-error in 6/6 option sets, the generator (517-550 per seed) and the fuzzer (42 H). KFOLD64: t_rec, generator, fuzzer (H and U), t_jit2, and the fix1 part through its results. INEXACT-JIT (no result guard): generator, t_rec, t_jit2, fuzzer H. FIX1: only the fix1 part.

INEXACT-RECABORT is not measured by me. [I] My differential suites probably cannot catch it: the result guard still raises, so the only effect is coverage. C3 should measure it or drop the arm and say why.
Linux was not run. r3/b has no Linux B luajit. The scripts are POSIX sh: cygpath and timeout are used only when present, and awk and sed use portable patterns, but this is untested off MSYS.

Campaign sizes are for the main session to choose. Examples: OCLJ_BITJIT_SEED=101 OCLJ_BITJIT_SEEDS=20 (about 3.5 min, about 9 MB a seed) plus the same with OCLJ_BITJIT_GENMODE=phi; the fuzzer at OCLJ_BITFUZZ_SEED=11 OCLJ_BITFUZZ_SEEDS=50 OCLJ_BITFUZZ_CASES=20000 writes about 6.3 GB unpruned. Whether to prune is the user's call.

t_rec has no PUC comparison, and the task said only 'where they have one', so I did not add one. Under B, 40-47% of t_rec's runs raise, mostly within 5 iterations [M: 804-949 of 2000; 76-107 after iteration 60]. It still catches NARROW, KFOLD64, INEXACT-JIT and SELFGUARD.

Windows luajit.exe and lua.exe write CRLF to stdout. The runners strip CR before every comparison. Anyone comparing outputs by hand should do the same: in one of my ad-hoc diffs, grep's CR handling produced 25 false differences.
